recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-27917 unless generated publication artifacts outside source control are later found stale; future generation should continue to derive BTG from the current XML source.
issue_request: FHIR-27917 was Published/Persuasive for R5 and requested changing the Purpose of Use code in the OperationOutcome break-the-glass examples from ETREAT to its child code BTG.
initial_application: No local commit explicitly tagged FHIR-27917 was found. The example was originally added in 2015 with ETREAT, and commit db9b233cd7a1a0059f4e30f581456e27d34b5a36 later changed source/operationoutcome/operationoutcome-example-break-the-glass.xml to BTG/Break the glass, apparently applying the requested source change under a commit subject for another tracker.
additional_context: OperationOutcome is active in source/fhir.ini and the break-glass example is listed in source/operationoutcome/list-OperationOutcome-examples.xml, so the XML source drives the generated example formats referenced by Jira. The break-glass narrative moved from security-labels.html to security.html under FHIR-53885, and the current security page consistently references v3-ActReason#BTG. FHIR-I minutes for 2020-10-26 corroborate the Persuasive 11-0-0 decision; community searches found no conflicting evidence.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The authoritative OperationOutcome example already uses http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/v3-ActReason#BTG with display Break the glass, and searches found no ETREAT occurrence in the relevant OperationOutcome or security break-glass source files.
